score.note: First structural draft, not a permutation search, of a genuinely one-off owner: the family-transplant tool's family-matcher assigned games/gs1/src/battle/effects/member_orbit/run.c (main:080ce85c, score 7743/10000) as the closest structural template, and the m2c workbench produced no assisted context at all ('Function not found') -- worked directly from a full manual byte-offset decode of games/gs1/asm/080d9ae8.s (built with a small local script resolving every pc-relative literal-pool load to its value and every branch to its label, cross-checked internally by confirming every resolved pool target lands inside an actual .4byte block, never mid-instruction) plus the sibling evidence named in the task brief. Confirmed owner_bytes is 1248, not 1180 as an early buggy version of the decode script reported (the bug: matching 'bl ' with a literal space against tab-separated source text, undercounting each of the 34 `bl` sites by 2 bytes -- 34*2=68, and 1180+68=1248 exactly, which is what caught the bug). The template match is real but partial: this owner shares the whole 0x03001eec work-block calling shape (Func_080cd594/Func_080e0524/Func_08002f40/Func_080041d8/Func_08004278/Func_08002dd8/Func_080cdbc0) and several field offsets with 080ce85c, but is NOT an orbit effect -- it is a distinct 'palette ramp' effect (confirmed by the already-assigned name RunPaletteRampEffect in games/gs1/source-paths.json and by the four already-adopted battle/effects/palette_ramp/mode_N.c callers, which fixed the signature as `s32 RunPaletteRampEffect(s32 effect, s32 mode)`) with its own two-phase structure: (1) an 8-step brightness-clamped-copy 'ramp' table built once at work+0x2580 (7 shaded copies of a 696-byte source image, ceiling stepping 57,50,...,15), a 512-slot particle-ring seeded with mode-dependent angle buckets, then (2) a member_count*4+64-pass animation loop where each of up to member_count members runs on its own frame offset staggered by -4 per member index (both a `local_frame` and a `threshold` loop-carried variable decremented together), drawing one member-position sprite via Func_08004cb4/Func_080e3944 while local_frame>0 (size/table selection depends on `mode`), and, once threshold falls in [0,36], drawing all 24 of that member's ramp-buffer-relative burst particles from a per-member 896-byte particle sub-range. Two `bl Func_080072f4` sites (both inside the burst-particle draw, one inside the mode==0 single-sprite draw, one inside the mode!=1 single-sprite draw -- three total) are the `_call_via_r4` trampoline (games/gs1/asm/080072e4.s, N=4 slot), modeled as indirect DrawRectangleFn calls through `callback_pair[0]`/`callback_pair[1]` per the already-established 080dc1ec.c/080e01e4.c idiom, with callback_pair populated by the already-adopted Func_080cef64 (games/gs1/src/unidentified/main/runtime/runtime_owner_21.c). Iterated five times against --align: (1) fixed a missing `Func_080cef64(effect->field4, callback_pair)` call omitted from the first draft entirely; (2) the mode-1-vs-else palette-id selection (`&Value_000000b7` vs `&Value_000000bb`) needed a nested `if (mode==0){bb}else if(mode==1){b7}else{bb}` -- a flat `mode!=0 && mode==1` short-circuit compiled down to a single comparison, dropping the reference's genuine two-compare/shared-else shape; (3) the 8-step ramp loop needed its ceiling (57,50,...) and destination-offset (696,1392,...) expressed as loop-carried accumulators decremented/incremented by a constant each pass, not recomputed via `64 - outer*7` / `outer*696` multiplication each iteration; (4) removed a hoisted `member_count` local whose one-time `M2C_FIELD(work+0x7828)->20` read was getting globally CSE'd by this compiler across unrelated later reads of the same field, per the family's documented 'always re-read via a fresh M2C_FIELD expression' guidance; (5) the two radius-scaled sin/cos particle-seed multiplies needed the *runtime* `radius` local (=192) explicitly on both sides matching the reference's real `muls` instruction and operand order (`radius * cos_val` for particle[4] but `sin_val * radius` for particle[5] -- an asymmetry the reference genuinely has), instead of the literal `192` which this compiler strength-reduces into shift/add sequences since it is a compile-time constant. A sixth fix, confirmed correct against the raw disassembly's own register trace (r5 = sp+64 for the Func_08004cb4 call, then immediately reassigned to sp+76 as a DIFFERENT address for the Func_080e3944 destination, never re-read from sp+64 afterward), replaced an incorrect two-buffer model (reusing one `rec[3]` local as both the Func_08004cb4 input AND the Func_080e3944 output) with the correct three-buffer model (`rec` camera-setup input, `screen` transform output reused by both the per-member and per-particle Func_080e3944 calls via the reference's persistent fp-held pointer, `zero_vec` a freshly-zeroed {0,0,0} input for the first call only) -- this is a real correctness fix, not a permutation, but it moved differing_halfwords from 505 to 558 (candidate_bytes 1224->1216, stack frame sub sp #88->#96, still short of the reference's #100 by one word) because it disturbed downstream register allocation broadly; kept per this family's established precedent (see 080dc1ec.json prior_note_2026_08_27b/d) that a metric regression traced to a genuine semantic fix is not grounds to revert to the wrong model. Net movement from the first working draft: differing_halfwords 581->558 and wrong_instructions 460->460 (unchanged at the endpoints, but not flat in between -- fixes 1-5 alone dropped it to a low of 420/505 before the buffer-model fix's cascading stack-offset renumbering pushed the raw diff-line count back up to 460/558 despite the underlying code being more correct, not less; see the buffer-model entry in rejected_experiments for why this was kept anyway).

family.template_note: The family-matcher's closest structural template by score (7743/10000), and genuinely useful for the shared 0x03001eec work-block calling shape, the M2C_FIELD/heap_cache/cursor-advance idiom, and the DrawRectangleFn/WordCopyFn typedefs -- but not a control-flow match. Owner sizes differ (1248 vs member_orbit's bytes) and confirmed by direct decode: this owner is a two-phase 'palette ramp' effect (brightness-clamped image copies plus a 512-slot particle ring, then a per-member staggered draw-and-burst animation loop), not member_orbit's single per-frame 4-sprite-per-member orbit loop. No m2c-assisted context existed for this owner (out/family-transplants/main-080d9ae8/m2c/ absent, 'Function not found'), so the template served only as a style reference, not a structural starting point.

rejected_experiments: `if (mode != 0 && mode == 1) {...} else {...}` for the palette-id selection: this compiler folds the redundant `mode != 0` guard away (provably implied by `mode == 1`), collapsing the reference's genuine two-comparison/shared-else shape into one `cmp`. Replaced with an explicit `if (mode==0){bb} else if (mode==1){b7} else {bb}`, which reproduces both comparisons and a single shared else target without any cross-jumping needed (the two `bb` arms are never separately materialized -- confirmed the compiler treats the trailing `else` as the sole physical target for both the `mode==0` and `mode!=1` exits).

Ramp-loop ceiling/destination-offset computed via `64 - outer*7` / `work+0x2580+outer*696` (fresh multiplication from the outer loop index each pass): produced extra `movs`/scheduling noise not present in the reference, which visibly accumulates both values via `-=7`/`+=696` at the loop bottom instead. Switched to loop-carried accumulators.

A separately named `member_count` local, read once via `M2C_FIELD(work+0x7828)->20` before the `!= -64` pre-check and left otherwise unused: this compiler's CSE recognized the identical field-access text reappearing at the loop-exit condition and the inner-loop entry guard and started caching the `work+0x7828` pointer sum across the whole per-frame loop in a persistent register/stack slot, diverging sharply from the reference's fresh-reload-every-site pattern. Removed; every member_count-adjacent site now uses its own fresh M2C_FIELD expression, per the family's established guidance.

Literal `192 * Func_0800231c(angle)` / `192 * Func_08002322(angle)` for the two particle-seed multiplies: this compiler strength-reduces a compile-time-constant multiplicand into shift/add sequences (`(x<<1+x)<<6`), not the reference's real `muls` instruction. Introduced a genuine runtime `radius = 192;` local instead, which restores the `muls`; the two calls also needed opposite operand order (`radius * cos_val` vs `sin_val * radius`) to match the reference's own asymmetry.

Reusing one `rec[3]` local as both the Func_08004cb4 camera-setup input and (after that call returns) the Func_080e3944 per-member screen-position output: plausible from the field-offset shape alone, but the raw disassembly's register trace disproves it -- r5 holds sp+64 for the Func_08004cb4 call, then is immediately reassigned to a genuinely different address (sp+76) for the Func_080e3944 destination and is never re-read from sp+64 afterward, and that same sp+76 pointer (via `mov fp,r5`) is what the later burst-loop's per-particle Func_080e3944 calls reuse as their output too. Replaced with three separate locals (`rec`, `screen`, `zero_vec`); this is a confirmed correctness fix even though it temporarily worsened the raw differing_halfwords count via cascading register-allocation changes -- not reverted, matching this family's established 'small metric regression traded for real correctness' precedent (see games/gs1/recon/en/main/080dc1ec.json).

Explicit `facing_end = facing + 12;` local hoisted once before the member loop, replacing two inline `facing + 12` expressions: zero measured effect on the compiled output (byte-identical score before and after) -- kept anyway as a source-fidelity improvement since the reference does store this value to its own stack slot once per outer frame, even though this compiler happens to produce the same code either way.

Semantic summary: a two-phase battle-presentation 'palette ramp' sub-effect taking (effect, mode). Phase 1 (once): stores effect at work+0x7828, sets BG2 affine scale, registers a mode-selected startup effect id, loads a mode-selected palette to 0x05000000, loads a 696-byte source image into work+0x2580 and builds 7 additional brightness-clamped copies of it immediately after (ceiling 57 down to 15 in steps of 7), computes a y_offset from effect->field4, then seeds a fixed 512-slot particle ring at 0x02010000 with mode-dependent angle-bucket fields and a radius-192 sin/cos position. Phase 2: `member_count*4+64` animation passes; each pass re-fetches `facing`, fires a one-shot sound at frame 72, then walks every party member with that member's own frame offset (`local_frame`) staggered -4 per member index. While `local_frame>0`, draws one member-position sprite (size/table depends on `mode`, drawn through one of two DrawRectangleFn callbacks resolved once via Func_080cef64). Once the member's `threshold` (also staggered -4 per member) falls in [0,36], draws all 24 of a per-member 896-byte particle sub-range using a burst index (0, or `(local_frame-24)/4` clamped to 7) to pick which of the 8 ramp-buffer brightness copies to sample, indexed further by two 12-entry byte tables (Data_080eea20/2c, width/height) and a 12-entry halfword table (Data_080eea08, source offset).
No GS2 or external source was used; no other Golden Sun decompilation project was consulted.
